whatIsIt.eli5: Two teachers. One lets many squares answer for each weed (good for learning); the other lets only one square answer (good for final use).
whatIsIt.simple: End-to-end models train two copies of the head. The one-to-many copy uses TAL with 10 positives per object; the one-to-one copy gets exactly one positive per object. Only the one-to-one copy is needed at inference, so no NMS.
whatIsIt.engineer: Consistent dual assignment (YOLOv10): shared features, o2m head with top-k = 10, o2o head with top-1 using the same alignment metric so both heads agree. In Ultralytics' E2ELoss the o2o assigner uses topk = 7 then topk2 = 1.

whyExists.eli5: Learning with many helpers is easier, but at the end you want one answer per weed.
whyExists.simple: One-to-many gives rich training signal; one-to-one removes duplicates at the source. Training both gets both benefits.
whyExists.engineer: o2m provides dense supervision; o2o enables NMS-free inference; the consistent metric minimises the supervision gap.

eli5: Both teachers grade the same guesses.
The many-answers teacher helps the model learn.
The one-answer teacher makes the final answers clean.
simple: Both heads read the same neck features.
At inference only the one-to-one head runs its outputs into the final list.
engineer: YOLO26 'Progressive Loss' in Ultralytics' E2ELoss: loss = w·L_o2m + (1−w)·L_o2o with w decaying linearly from 0.8 to 0.1 over training.
